evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Card information, discards and exhaustion
evidence.text: If the cosmic deck runs out, reshuffle available discards. If a needed draw has no deck or discards, a **Cosmic Quake** makes everyone discard their hands; shuffle and deal eight to each player. If still insufficient, **Cosmic Aftershock** gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes Game Setup card holdings as at setup (including Miser's hoard). This is a needed-draw exhaustion rule, not an optional hand refresh.

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text: Each player leads an alien trying to establish five **foreign colonies**. A colony is one or more ships of one color on one planet; extra ships on that planet do not make extra colonies. Several colors can coexist there, each with its own colony. Home colonies are in your own system; foreign colonies are outside it. Five foreign planets can all be in one other system. Alien powers override conflicting general rules.

evidence.heading: Actions / Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal
evidence.text: Both sides' allies return ships to their own colonies, gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal. The main players have **one minute**. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other **one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony**, including a foreign colony. The recipient can use any own ships not in the warp. Existing ships coexist; the giver need not vacate, and vacating would eliminate the colony being offered. Return any remaining gate ships to offense's colonies.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target. The owner of a home system defends their planet even with zero ships there. Other colors' colonies are **bystanders**: they add nothing to the defense and the encounter result does not harm them. When driving out a foreign colony, target only that one color's colony; all other colors are bystanders.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

evidence.heading: Actions / Flare system
evidence.text: Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
